ticket: Add a script `tools/list_commands.py` that prints the name of every command documented in `skill/references/commands.md`, one per line, in file order. A command is a `### <name>` heading; headings that are not commands, such as `### Review rounds` and `### The scope check`, are left out. Add `tests/test_list_commands.py`, a unittest that runs the script and checks that `version`, `doctor` and `launch` are listed in that order. Change nothing else.

edits.tools/list_commands.py:
"""Print every command documented in skill/references/commands.md, one per line, in file order."""
import re
from pathlib import Path

DOC = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "skill" / "references" / "commands.md"


def commands(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Each `### <name>` heading that names a command: one or two lowercase words, not "the ..."."""
    out = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = re.fullmatch(r"### ([a-z][a-z-]*(?: [a-z][a-z-]*)?)", line.strip())
        if m and not m.group(1).startswith("the "):
            out.append(m.group(1))
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("\n".join(commands(DOC.read_text())))
edits.tests/test_list_commands.py:
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


class ListCommands(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_it_lists_documented_commands_in_order(self):
        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "list_commands.py")], capture_output=True,
                             text=True, check=True).stdout.splitlines()
        for name in ("version", "doctor", "launch"):
            self.assertIn(name, out)
        self.assertLess(out.index("version"), out.index("doctor"))
        self.assertLess(out.index("doctor"), out.index("launch"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
